# `orbit`

<!-- Generated by `vidgen gallery`; edit the sample in AGENTS.md (or video.yaml), not this file. -->

**Use it for:** planets, moons, satellites or a comet on their orbits, moving in correct timing (Kepler's laws, the inner planets for a year, the ISS and a geostationary orbit, a flyby); mutual gravity; manoeuvres: burns, Hohmann / bi-elliptic / phasing transfers with their Δv, phase angle and launch windows, a gravity assist; many bodies: Lagrange points and Trojans in the rotating frame, the figure-eight, binary stars, the Io–Europa–Ganymede resonance, tides (a schematic); the Solar System on a date (1800–2050), the next opposition or conjunction, all planets on a log scale, an inset of the inner planets, planet sizes to scale.

Orbits in correct timing: a central body (`central`: a preset or your own) and `bodies` on Kepler orbits (presets, elements, or a position and velocity), drawn as conics with the bodies moving along them through the whole scene at one speed-up (`span` or `orbits` of simulated time), fading trails, an equal-aspect frame in AU or km (`frame`: axes, a scale bar or none), a side panel with the time, speed-up and a legend, `follow` to move with a body, `dynamics: nbody` for mutual gravity (leapfrog, with the energy error shown). Kepler's laws and orbital speed: a body's `geometry` (foci, a, b, apsides), `sectors` (equal areas in equal times) and `velocity` (vectors, vis-viva speed); `cannonball` (Newton's cannon: one point, increasing speeds). Manoeuvres: a body's `burns` (Δv prograde, radial, normal...), a `transfer` (Hohmann, bi-elliptic, phasing: Δv₁, Δv₂, transfer time, phase angle, launch windows), a `flyby` (a gravity assist in the planet's frame with the Sun-frame vector diagram).

## YAML

From the author guide (`vidgen guide scenes`):

```yaml
- id: inner_planets
  type: orbit   # bodies move by Kepler's equation at one speed-up from the first beat to the scene's end
  params:
    title: "The inner planets for one Earth year"
    central: sun   # a preset (sun, earth, mars, jupiter...) or {name, gm or mass, radius}
    bodies:        # presets: mercury ... neptune (JPL J2000 elements), moon, iss, geo, halley
      - {preset: mercury}
      - {preset: earth}
      - {name: Comet, a: "1.5 AU", e: 0.7, argp: 180, nu: 180, trail: 0.15}   # values carry units; angles in degrees
    span: "1 yr"   # or orbits: 2 (periods of the first body)
    caption: "J2000 elements (JPL approximate positions)"
  beats:
    - text: "Mercury races around the Sun in eighty-eight days."
    - text: "The comet crawls far out and sweeps past the Sun."
```

| `bodies.r` | `list[str \| float] \| None` |  | Start position relative to what it orbits, instead of elements: ['1 AU', 0] or [x, y, z] with units. |
| `bodies.v` | `list[str \| float] \| None` |  | Start velocity with r: [0, '29.8 km/s']. |
| `bodies.gm` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Its own gravitational parameter (matters for n-body and adds to its parent's in μ = G(M + m)); default 0 (a probe) or the preset's. |

| `bodies.radius` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Its radius ('1737 km'); drawn to scale when large enough. |
| `bodies.label` | `str` |  | Text shown next to it (default: its name). |

| `bodies.velocity.along` | `int` | `0` | Also this many fixed arrows along the orbit at equal times (crowded where it is slow, long where it is fast). |
| `bodies.velocity.readout` | `bool` | `True` | The speed now (vis-viva, v² = μ(2/r − 1/a)) and its range, fastest at periapsis, in the readout. |
| `bodies.alongside` | `str \| None` |  | Start where another body listed before is, moving with it ('Earth': a spacecraft leaving with the planet), instead of elements. |
| `bodies.burns` | `list[OrbitBurn]` |  | Impulsive burns, in time order: [{at: '45 min', prograde: '0.5 km/s'}, {at: apoapsis, prograde: '0.4 km/s'}]; each Δv drawn as an arrow at its point, the orbits before and after. |
| `bodies.burns.at` | `str \| float` | `0.0` | When: a time from the start ('45 min'; 0 the start), or periapsis / apoapsis (the next one after the burn before). |
| `bodies.burns.prograde` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Δv along the velocity ('2.4 km/s'): faster, the far side of the orbit rises. |
| `bodies.burns.retrograde` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Δv against the velocity: slower, the far side sinks. |
| `bodies.burns.radial` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Δv in the orbit's plane, perpendicular to the velocity, outwards: turns the orbit (the apsides move). |

| `bodies.burns.normal` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Δv out of the plane, along the angular momentum: tilts the orbit (a plane change; seen from above the picture shows only its projection). |
| `bodies.burns.anti_normal` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Δv out of the plane the other way. |
| `bodies.burns.label` | `str` |  | Text next to its Δv arrow (default: Δv₁ 2.43 km/s prograde). |
| `bodies.near` | `'L1' \| 'L2' \| 'L3' \| 'L4' \| 'L5' \| None` |  | With a three-body system: start at this Lagrange point (L1…L5), at rest in the rotating frame (a Trojan near L4). |

| `bodies.drift` | `list[float \| str] \| None` |  | With near: a starting velocity [x, y] in the rotating frame: numbers are shares of the secondary's orbital speed, or speeds ('0.1 km/s'). |
| `bodies.curvature` | `bool` | `False` | Check which way its path bends around the central body (the Moon's path around the Sun is always concave towards it): the result in the panel. |

| `cannonball.show_paths` | `bool` | `False` | Draw each shot's whole path faintly from the start (the trajectories to come). |

| `transfer.kind` | `'hohmann' \| 'bielliptic' \| 'phasing'` | `'hohmann'` | hohmann (two burns, half an ellipse), bielliptic (three burns, out to apoapsis and back in), phasing (catch up a body on the same orbit). |
| `transfer.ship` | `str` | required | The body that flies it (listed in bodies, on a circular orbit; alongside: Earth starts it with a planet). |

| `flyby.periapsis` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Closest distance to the planet's centre ('400000 km'); or altitude. |
| `flyby.altitude` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Closest height above the surface ('200000 km'). |
| `flyby.side` | `'behind' \| 'in_front'` | `'behind'` | behind: the probe passes behind the planet (on the side it comes from) and gains speed around the Sun; in_front: it loses speed. |
| `flyby.angle` | `str \| float` | `150.0` | Direction of v∞ coming in, in degrees from the planet's motion (180: straight against it; 150: mostly from ahead). |
| `flyby.planet_speed` | `str \| float \| None` |  | The planet's speed around the Sun ('13.06 km/s'); default: a preset planet's circular speed at its mean distance. |
| `flyby.atmosphere` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Height of the top of the atmosphere ('100 km'): a periapsis in it is refused. |
| `flyby.name` | `str` | `'Probe'` | The probe's name (target body:<name>). |
| `flyby.reach` | `float \| None` |  | How far out the pass starts and ends, in periapsis distances; default: far enough to show where the asymptotes cross (at least 6). |
| `flyby.vectors` | `bool` | `True` | Draw the Sun-frame vector diagram: the planet's velocity plus v∞ before and after. |
| `span` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Simulated time the scene shows ('1 yr', '92 min', '30 d'); or orbits. |

| `method` | `str` | `'leapfrog'` | n-body method: leapfrog (velocity Verlet, symplectic: energy error bounded) or rk45 (adaptive; drifts over long runs; the default with a three-body pair, whose small body may pass close to the secondary). |
| `step` | `str \| float \| None` |  | n-body leapfrog step ('1 h'); default 1/1000 of the shortest orbital time scale. |

| `unit` | `'auto' \| 'AU' \| 'km'` | `'auto'` | Unit of the axes and scale bar; auto: AU when the view spans more than 0.05 AU, else km. |
| `extent` | `str \| float \| None` |  | Half-width of the view around its centre ('2 AU'); default: every orbit with a margin. |
| `follow` | `str \| None` |  | A body the view moves with (its satellites' orbits stay still around it); default: the central body stays at the centre. |

| `energy` | `bool \| None` |  | Show the n-body energy error ΔE/E (default: on with dynamics: nbody). |

| `label_size` | `size \| None` |  | Size of tick labels, body labels and the readout (never below the readable minimum); default: caption (the picture gets the room). |
| `caption` | `str` |  | Note under the picture (e.g. the source of the elements); in 16:9 under the side panel when the column has room. |
| `caption_size` | `size` | `'caption'` | Caption text size. |
| `caption_color` | `color` | `'dim'` | Caption color. |
| `title_size` | `size` | `'heading'` | Title size. (also: heading_size) |
| `title_color` | `color` | `'text'` | Title color. (also: heading_color) |
| `system` | `OrbitSystem \| None` |  | Many bodies (Step 232): a circular restricted three-body pair — earth_moon, sun_earth, sun_jupiter, or {primary: sun, secondary: jupiter, mu: 0.05} — integrated with every body near it (n-body), or figure_eight (three equal masses, Chenciner–Montgomery). |
| `system.preset` | `str \| None` |  | earth_moon, sun_earth (the Sun with the Earth–Moon barycentre), sun_jupiter (restricted three-body pairs) or figure_eight (three equal masses). |
| `system.primary` | `str \| None` |  | The larger body of a pair of your own (a preset body: sun, earth, jupiter...). |
| `system.secondary` | `str \| None` |  | The smaller body of the pair (a preset body); it goes round the primary on a circle. |
| `system.mu` | `float \| None` |  | The mass ratio μ = m₂/(m₁ + m₂) instead of the bodies' own (the secondary's mass is set from it): L4 and L5 are stable below 0.0385 (Routh). |
| `system.separation` | `str \| float \| None` |  | The distance between the primaries ('5.2 AU'); default: the secondary preset's mean distance. |
| `system.mass` | `str \| float \| None` |  | figure_eight: each body's mass ('1 Msun'). |
| `system.scale` | `str \| float \| None` |  | figure_eight: the length the published unit stands for ('1 AU'): the eight is about 2.2 of it wide. |
| `view` | `'inertial' \| 'rotating'` | `'inertial'` | With a three-body pair: inertial (the pair goes round) or rotating (the frame turns with the pair: both stand still, the Lagrange points too); the actions corotate and inertial switch on a word. |
| `origin` | `'central' \| 'barycentre' \| None` |  | What stays at the centre of the view: the central body, or the barycentre of the bodies with mass (default with system; a binary star: both stars go round it). |
| `lagrange` | `bool \| list['L1' \| 'L2' \| 'L3' \| 'L4' \| 'L5']` | `False` | With a three-body pair: mark the Lagrange points (true: L1–L5, or some of them) computed for its mass ratio; their distances and Routh's stability test in the panel. |
| `zero_velocity` | `bool \| str` | `False` | With a three-body pair: draw the zero-velocity curve of a body placed near a Lagrange point (true: the first), for its Jacobi constant: it cannot cross it. |
| `resonance` | `OrbitResonance \| None` |  | A mean-motion resonance: [Io, Europa, Ganymede] or {bodies, conjunctions, keep}: period ratios, the Laplace angle of a 1:2:4 chain, conjunctions marked as they happen. |
| `resonance.bodies` | `list[str]` | required | Two or three bodies around the same body, inner first: their period ratios (and the Laplace angle of a 1:2:4 chain) in the panel. |
| `resonance.conjunctions` | `bool` | `True` | Mark each conjunction of neighbours (a line from the centre through both) as it happens: they recur at nearly the same places. |
| `resonance.keep` | `int` | `6` | How many past conjunctions of each pair stay drawn (faint). |
| `center` | `str \| None` |  | Centre the view on where this body is halfway through the span (with extent: a close-up; the central body far off is shown by an arrow at the edge). |
| `tides` | `OrbitTides \| bool \| None` |  | The tidal schematic (true or {satellite: moon, locking, points}): the satellite's pull at points of the planet, the differential (tidal) arrows, the two bulges, tidal locking; labelled schematic, not to scale. |
| `tides.satellite` | `str` | `'moon'` | The body raising the tides (a preset orbiting the central body: moon, io...). |
| `tides.locking` | `bool` | `True` | Show the satellite's near side marked: it spins once per orbit (tidal locking), so the same face looks at the planet. |
| `tides.points` | `int` | `12` | How many points around the planet carry arrows. |
| `date` | `str \| date \| None` |  | The Solar System on a date (Step 233): '2020-10-13' (1800–2050) places the planet presets (and Pluto) by JPL's approximate elements and rates on that day; the panel shows the date as the clock runs. |
| `event` | `OrbitEvent \| None` |  | With date: the next conjunction / opposition after it, found by root finding — {kind: opposition, of: Mars} (observer: Earth) — drawn as the line they will stand on; default span: until a little after it. |
| `event.kind` | `'opposition' \| 'conjunction' \| 'inferior_conjunction' \| 'superior_conjunction' \| 'aligned'` | `'opposition'` | opposition (the outer planet opposite the Sun, seen from the observer), conjunction (behind the Sun), inferior_conjunction / superior_conjunction (an inner planet between / beyond), aligned (equal heliocentric longitudes). |
| `event.of` | `str` | required | The planet (a body of the scene: Mars). |
| `event.observer` | `str` | `'Earth'` | Where it is seen from (a body of the scene; default Earth). |
| `radial` | `'linear' \| 'log'` | `'linear'` | linear: true distances; log: distances compressed (log10(1 + r/r0)) so Mercury and Neptune fit one picture, with labelled rings instead of axes and 'distances compressed' in the panel. |
| `inset` | `bool \| str \| float \| None` |  | A box beside the picture with the inner Solar System to scale (true: the orbits within 2 AU, or a radius '1.8 AU'); the region it shows is dashed in the main picture. |
| `sizes` | `OrbitSizes \| bool \| None` |  | A picture of radii to scale side by side (true: the scene's bodies or the eight planets; {bodies: [earth, moon, mars], sun: true}), the Sun's edge first; distances are not shown. |
| `sizes.bodies` | `list[str] \| None` |  | Body presets to compare (mercury … neptune, pluto, moon, io…); default: the scene's bodies, or the eight planets. |
| `sizes.sun` | `bool` | `True` | Show the Sun's edge (to the same scale) when the central body is the Sun. |

## Targets

`title`, `frame`, `central`, `body:<name>`, `orbit:<name>`, `geometry:<name>`, `foci:<name>`, `axes:<name>`, `periapsis:<name>`, `apoapsis:<name>`, `sectors:<name>`, `velocity:<name>`, `cannon`, `shot:<n>`, `burn:<n>`, `transfer`, `phase`, `asymptotes`, `turn`, `v_inf`, `motion`, `atmosphere`, `vectors`, `v_before`, `v_after`, `lagrange`, `lagrange:<L>`, `zero_velocity`, `rotation`, `barycentre`, `conjunctions`, `pointer`, `pull`, `mean`, `tidal`, `bulges`, `face`, `event`, `inset`, `rings`, `readout`
